about: Maps three.js APIs to their null3D equivalents. Each entry gives a status, the first engine version and a docs page ID.

statusLegend.direct: Same concept; the call or option changes name only.
statusLegend.changed: Supported, with a different API or pattern. Follow the note.
statusLegend.manual: Must be rewritten by hand, for example GLSL shaders or render hooks.
statusLegend.post-1.0: Not in version 1.0. Use the workaround in the note.
statusLegend.unsupported: Out of scope for null3D. Use the workaround in the note.

sinceLegend.0.1: the core renderer, with cameras, materials, lights and shadows
sinceLegend.0.2: content, such as glTF models, animation, raycasting and post-processing
sinceLegend.0.3: developer tools, such as the `null3d` command, templates and the porting tools

entries.target: createEngine({ canvas, sketch }) on the page; scene code moves to sketch.ts inside defineSketch()
entries.notes: The engine picks WebGPU or WebGL2 itself. antialias maps to the quality preset (MSAA 4x from Medium); alpha: true maps to createEngine({ transparent: true }); powerPreference maps to createEngine({ powerPreference }), whose default is 'high-performance'.

entries.target: createEngine({ maxPixelRatio }) and the quality presets
entries.notes: Presets cap the pixel ratio (1.5 on Low, 2 on Medium and High). Dynamic resolution then adjusts the render scale.

entries.three: renderer.setSize / window resize handler / camera.aspect + updateProjectionMatrix
entries.target: Automatic
entries.notes: The engine follows the canvas's CSS size. Perspective cameras, and orthographic cameras made with a height, follow its aspect ratio in every frame. Delete resize handlers and updateProjectionMatrix calls.

entries.target: onUpdate(dt) returned from defineSketch()
entries.notes: The engine renders every frame by itself; never call a render function. Per-frame logic goes in onUpdate, camera-follow logic in onLateUpdate.

entries.target: castShadows: true on the light; filtering follows the preset
entries.notes: Presets use 3 x 3 or 5 x 5 PCF filtering. VSM has no equivalent.

entries.three: renderer.toneMapping (ACESFilmic, AgX, Neutral, Reinhard, Cineon, Linear) / toneMappingExposure
entries.target: post.set({ toneMapping: 'aces' | 'agx' | 'neutral' | 'none', exposure })
entries.notes: The engine default is ACES; three.js defaults to no tone mapping, so ports of scenes without it set toneMapping: "none". Reinhard and Cineon have no built-in equivalent: use "neutral", or a custom final effect (0.2).

entries.target: Nothing to do
entries.notes: Output is sRGB with a linear working space, as in three.js r152+ defaults. Hex colors are read as sRGB, as three.js does. Delete these lines.

entries.target: debug.stats(true); debug.frameStats() for numbers
entries.notes: The overlay shows frame phases per thread, GPU tier and preset.

entries.target: await scene.warmUp() before hiding the loading screen
entries.notes: The first frame waits for its pipelines. warmUp resolves once every pipeline that the scene needs is built, hidden objects included, so warm up a later loading stage before you show it.

entries.target: scene.setBackground('#rrggbb' | texture | environment)
createEngine({ canvas })
entries.notes: Create the canvas in HTML or in page.ts and pass it in. The engine hands it to the render worker.

entries.target: await engine.capture() on the page
entries.notes: Returns an image of the next complete frame. Tests use the engine's readback instead.

entries.target: render.addPass({ kind: 'scene', camera, writes: 'myTexture', size }) and sample 'myTexture' in a material
entries.notes: Passes are declared, not called: the render graph orders them and manages their memory.

entries.three: renderer.setViewport / setScissor (split screens, picture in picture)
entries.target: A render-to-texture pass plus a final effect, for minimaps and picture in picture (0.2)
entries.notes: Several full views (scene.createView), such as split screens, come after 1.0.

entries.target: engine.capabilities on the page, which sends the sketch what it needs with engine.postToSketch
entries.notes: Reports GPU tier, limits and features. Never branch on GPU names: some browsers hide them.

entries.target: Nothing to do; createEngine({ largeWorld: true }) for planet-scale scenes
entries.notes: The engine draws reversed depth in a 32-bit float buffer on WebGPU, and on WebGL2 where the browser has EXT_clip_control. engine.capabilities.depth says which depth the device draws. The engine also renders relative to the camera through per-cell offsets.

entries.target: The scene from the sketch context: defineSketch(({ scene }) => ...)
entries.notes: Objects are created in the scene directly.

entries.target: scene.setEnvironment(await assets.loadEnvironment('/env/studio.ktx2'))
entries.notes: Prefilter HDR files offline with `bunx @null3d/cli assets env`. A built-in neutral studio environment replaces RoomEnvironment: assets.builtinEnvironment('studio').

entries.three: scene.fog = new Fog(color, near, far) / new FogExp2(color, density)
entries.target: scene.setFog({ type: 'linear', color, near, far }) or { type: 'exp2', color, density }
entries.notes: Materials opt out with fog: false.

entries.target: scene.createGroup({ name, position })
child.setParent(parent); setParent(parent, { keepWorld: true }) for attach(); destroy() to remove
entries.notes: Objects are in the scene as soon as they are created. setParent keeps the local transform, like add(). Creating, destroying and re-parenting rebuild the draw tables in that frame, so during play hide with setVisible and pool with setActiveCount instead (guides/performance).

entries.target: obj.setPosition(x, y, z); obj.translate(x, y, z) for translateX/Y/Z
entries.notes: translate moves along the object's own axes, as translateX, translateY and translateZ do together. For many moving objects, write instance-batch or dynamic arrays directly instead of calling setters.

entries.target: obj.setRotationEuler(x, y, z, 'XYZ'), obj.rotateX/Y/Z(angle), or obj.setRotation(qx, qy, qz, qw)
entries.notes: Euler order strings match three.js. rotateX, rotateY and rotateZ turn the object about its own axes, as in three.js. For rotateOnAxis, multiply the quaternion from obj.getRotation by one from quat.setAxisAngle, and pass the product to setRotation.

entries.target: obj.setRotation(x, y, z, w), with the quaternion from quat.setAxisAngle, quat.fromEuler, quat.multiply or quat.slerp
entries.notes: The quat helpers write into an array that you create once with quat.create(). Pass its four numbers to setRotation. The rotations array of an instance batch takes the same order.

entries.target: obj.setScale(x, y, z)
obj.lookAt(x, y, z)
entries.notes: Cameras look down -Z, as in three.js, and lights will too when they become objects later in 0.1.

entries.target: obj.getWorldPosition(out), obj.getWorldQuaternion(out), obj.getWorldMatrix(out)
entries.notes: Each getter copies into an array that you make once, with vec3.create(), quat.create() or mat4.create(). They read the last frame that the engine processed, so a change made in onUpdate shows from the next onUpdate on. getWorldMatrix gives 16 numbers, column by column, like matrixWorld.elements.

entries.target: Nothing to do: objects are static by default and update when a setter changes them; create objects that move every frame with dynamic: true
entries.notes: Remove manual matrix calls. Only dynamic objects and instance batches may be written through typed arrays.

entries.target: scene.find(name) for getObjectByName; your own arrays of objects instead of traverse and children
entries.notes: scene.find returns the first object created with the name, from an index. No call walks an object's children, so keep the objects you need in arrays at setup time.

entries.target: obj.setVisible(false)
entries.notes: Cheap: it uploads the object's matrix and draw entry and never rebuilds the draw tables, so use it instead of removing and adding objects during play.

entries.target: mesh.setCastShadows(true) / setReceiveShadows(true), or the castShadows and receiveShadows options of createMesh
entries.notes: Both are false by default, as in three.js. This version stores them but draws no shadows yet.

entries.target: obj.setLayers(mask), camera.setLayers(mask), batch.setLayers(mask); the layers option of createMesh, createInstances and createPerspectiveCamera
entries.notes: Masks have the same 32 bits and the same default, layer 0 alone, and a camera draws an object when their masks share a bit. layers.set(n) becomes setLayers(1 << n). For enable and disable, keep the mask in your code and pass the new mask. An InstancedMesh's layers become its batch's, for every row. Raycasts and declared passes take layer masks from 0.2.

entries.target: mesh.setRenderOrder(n)
entries.notes: Affects the order of transparent objects. The engine orders opaque objects itself for speed. This version draws every material opaque, so the order has no effect yet.

entries.target: mesh.setFrustumCulled(false)
entries.notes: Usually needed only for shader-displaced geometry; prefer mesh.setBounds(center, radius) with larger bounds, which keeps culling at work.

entries.target: Your own arrays, or a Map keyed by the object
entries.notes: Engine objects are not extensible. A Map from each object to its data keeps the data beside the object, and arrays indexed the way your sketch counts objects stay fastest in per-frame loops.

entries.target: onUpdate / onLateUpdate, or a declared pass
entries.notes: Sketch code never runs in the render worker, so per-draw callbacks cannot exist.

entries.target: scene.instantiate(prefab) for loaded models; scene.clone(obj) for built objects
entries.notes: Skinned models clone correctly with instantiate.

entries.target: destroy() on the engine object
entries.notes: texture.destroy() frees a texture's GPU memory, and materials that map it draw with their colors alone. A prefab (0.2) frees its GPU data when the prefab and its last instance are destroyed.

entries.target: render.addPass({ kind: 'scene', materialOverride }) or debug.view('normals')
scene.setEnvironment(env, { rotation }) and scene.setBackground(env, { rotation })
entries.notes: Rotation is an Euler array in radians, as in three.js.

entries.target: scene.setBackground(env, { blur, intensity })
scene.createPerspectiveCamera({ fov, near, far, position, target })
entries.notes: fov is vertical and in degrees, as in three.js. The aspect ratio is automatic. The fov, near and far properties are read-only: change them with camera.setFov(degrees) and camera.setNearFar(near, far).

entries.three: OrthographicCamera(left, right, top, bottom, near, far)
entries.target: scene.createOrthographicCamera({ height, near, far, position, target }), or left, right, top and bottom in place of height
entries.notes: With height alone, the width follows the canvas's aspect ratio, so code that recomputes left and right on resize goes away. The four edges keep their shape on any canvas, as in three.js. To zoom, call camera.setOrthoHeight with the original height divided by three.js's zoom.

entries.target: A static environment map, or reflection probes baked offline
None; split screens come after 1.0 with multiple views
entries.notes: Stereo rendering belongs to XR, which is out of scope.

entries.target: scene.createDirectionalLight({ direction, color, intensity, castShadows })
entries.notes: Shadow cascades fit the view automatically, so delete shadow.camera bounds and target updates.

entries.target: scene.createPointLight({ position, color, intensity, range, decay })
entries.notes: distance becomes range; 0 (infinite) is not allowed, because clustered lighting needs a range.

entries.three: SpotLight(color, intensity, distance, angle, penumbra, decay)
entries.target: scene.createSpotLight({ position, direction | target, angle, penumbra, range, intensity })
entries.notes: Spot light cookies (light.map) come after 1.0.

entries.target: scene.createHemisphereLight({ skyColor, groundColor, intensity })
scene.createAmbientLight({ color, intensity })
A spot light plus emissive geometry
scene.setEnvironment: diffuse spherical harmonics come with the environment
entries.notes: `bunx @null3d/cli assets env` computes them offline.

entries.target: Built in: shadow: { cascades } on the directional light
entries.notes: Delete the addon.

entries.target: shadow: { mapSize, bias, normalBias } in the light options
entries.notes: radius and blurSamples map to the preset's filter size; shadow.camera has no equivalent.

entries.target: Physical light units, as in three.js r155 and later
entries.notes: Scenes tuned in three.js's legacy light mode need new intensities: retune them with parity images.

entries.three: Box / Sphere / Plane / Cylinder / Cone / Torus / Capsule / Circle / Ring Geometry
entries.target: geometry.box({ width, height, depth }), geometry.sphere({ radius }), and one generator for each class
entries.notes: The constructor's arguments become options with the same names and defaults: new CylinderGeometry(0.3, 0.4, 2) is geometry.cylinder({ radiusTop: 0.3, radiusBottom: 0.4, height: 2 }). The meshes match three.js's vertex for vertex, with the same positions, normals, texture coordinates and triangles. Each object has one material, so an array of materials for the face groups of a box or a cylinder needs one object for each group.

entries.three: geometry.rotateX / rotateY / rotateZ / translate / scale / center / applyMatrix4
entries.target: obj.setRotationEuler(x, y, z), obj.setPosition(x, y, z) or obj.setScale(x, y, z) on the object that draws the mesh
entries.notes: A mesh keeps the vertices its generator built, so the transform goes on each object or instance row: floor.setRotationEuler(-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0) lays a plane flat. To build the transform into the vertices, transform the arrays and pass them to geometry.fromArrays.

entries.three: TorusKnot / Icosahedron / Octahedron / Tetrahedron / Dodecahedron / Polyhedron / Lathe / Extrude / Shape / Tube Geometry
entries.target: The same generators from @null3d/geometry
entries.notes: Same parameters as three.js; Shape and Path objects are ported too.

entries.target: geometry.fromArrays({ positions, normals, uvs, uvs1, colors, tangents, indices })
entries.notes: Returns a mesh that createMesh and createInstances accept. The attributes position, normal, uv, uv1, color and tangent each become one array, and setIndex becomes indices, 16-bit or 32-bit. The engine copies the arrays.

entries.target: meshAsset.updateVertices(name, data, start, count)
entries.notes: For many moving objects, use instances instead of rewriting vertices.

entries.target: geometry.fromArrays({ ..., computeNormals: true, computeTangents: true })
entries.notes: The results match three.js's bit for bit. computeTangents needs uvs, and works without indices too. Bounds are always automatic, so computeBoundingSphere and computeBoundingBox need no call.

entries.target: scene.createLines({ fromEdges: meshAsset, thresholdAngle }); debug.view('wireframe') for debugging
DOM labels (ui.trackLabel), a texture with pre-rendered text, or a text mesh baked into glTF
entries.notes: SDF text rendering comes after 1.0.

entries.target: glTF morph targets load automatically; obj.setMorphWeight(indexOrName, weight)
materials.standard({ color, map, metalness, roughness, normalMap, aoMap, emissive, ... })
entries.notes: See the materials reference for every parameter and its new name.

entries.three: MeshPhysicalMaterial (clearcoat, transmission, sheen, iridescence, anisotropy, specular)
entries.target: materials.standard for the base layer
entries.notes: Clearcoat, transmission, sheen and specular are planned for after 1.0. Until then, approximate them or write a surface function.

entries.target: materials.unlit({ color, map, opacity, alphaMode, vertexColors })
materials.standard with metalness 0 and roughness near 1 (Lambert), or roughness tuned to the Phong shininess
entries.notes: Expect small visual differences; check with parity images and accept or tune.

entries.target: A toon surface function (recipe in the materials reference)
debug.view('normals' | 'depth') for debugging; matcap is a surface-function recipe
materials.shader({ surface: wgslSource, uniforms, textures }) or a full WGSL shader
entries.notes: Rewrite in WGSL; prefer a surface function so lighting, shadows, fog and instancing keep working.

entries.target: A surface function or a vertex-offset function
entries.notes: The engine has no shader chunks to patch.

entries.target: WGSL surface functions
entries.notes: Most TSL nodes map to one WGSL expression; see the shader porting reference.

entries.three: transparent / opacity / alphaTest / side / depthWrite / depthTest / blending / vertexColors / flatShading
entries.target: alphaMode: 'blend' | 'mask' (with alphaCutoff), doubleSided, depthWrite, depthTest, blending: 'normal' | 'additive' | 'multiply', vertexColors, flatShading
entries.notes: transparent: true becomes alphaMode: 'blend'; alphaTest becomes alphaMode: 'mask' with alphaCutoff; side: DoubleSide becomes doubleSided: true. BackSide has no equivalent: flip the geometry.

entries.target: debug.view('wireframe') for debugging; scene.createLines({ fromEdges }) for production wireframes
entries.notes: WebGPU has no line-polygon mode, so wireframe is not a material flag.

entries.target: The scene environment; per-material envIntensity
Nothing to do
entries.notes: Options that change the shader, such as a normal map, are fixed when a material is created. Create each variant during loading: a new one compiles a pipeline, which can stall a frame.

entries.target: materials.shadowCatcher({ opacity })
fog: false in the material options
A normal map converted offline: `bunx @null3d/cli assets normal-from-bump`
entries.notes: Normal maps are cheaper at run time and look the same or better.

entries.target: A vertexOffset function that reads the texture with textureSampleLevel
entries.notes: Enlarge the object bounds with setBounds so culling does not hide displaced vertices.

entries.target: A surface function that sets s.alpha from the texture, or alpha packed into the base color map offline
entries.notes: three.js reads the alpha map from its green channel; keep that channel in the surface function.

entries.target: A surface function with alphaMode "mask" that sets alpha to 0 beyond the plane (cookbook recipe)
entries.notes: Shadows still use the unclipped mesh unless the shadow pass uses the same material.

entries.target: depthBias: { constant, slopeScale } in the material options
entries.notes: Signs differ because WebGPU uses reversed depth: the engine converts, so keep the three.js intent (push away from the camera).

entries.target: Put the objects on a layer drawn by a declared pass after the post chain (render graph, 0.2)
entries.notes: A per-material flag comes after 1.0; tone mapping runs once for the whole image.

entries.target: await assets.loadTexture(url, { colorSpace, flipY, wrap, filter, mipmaps, anisotropy, uvSet, premultipliedAlpha })
entries.notes: It returns a promise of the texture, which draws once its texels upload. flipY is true by default, as in three.js, and colorSpace is 'srgb'.

entries.target: colorSpace: 'srgb' for color maps, 'linear' for data maps
entries.notes: Same rule as three.js: base color and emissive maps are sRGB; normal, roughness, metalness and AO maps are linear. The default is 'srgb' for images and 'linear' for data. glTF sets them automatically.

entries.target: flipY in the loadTexture options
entries.notes: glTF textures never flip.

entries.three: wrapS / wrapT / repeat / offset / rotation / center
entries.target: wrap: 'repeat' | 'clamp' | 'mirror' in the texture options; repeat, offset and rotation go in the material's uvTransform
entries.notes: uvTransform follows glTF's KHR_texture_transform.

entries.target: filter: 'linear' | 'nearest', mipmaps, anisotropy (capped by the preset)
textures.fromData({ width, height, depth, format, data })
entries.notes: Formats rgba8unorm and rgba16float (a Uint16Array of half floats or a Float32Array). depth above 1 makes a texture array of that many layers. Filters are linear by default, where three.js's DataTexture is nearest: pass filter: 'nearest'.

entries.three: CanvasTexture (a 2D canvas redrawn at run time)
entries.target: Draw on an OffscreenCanvas in the sketch worker, then textures.fromImageBitmap(bitmap) and texture.update(bitmap)
entries.notes: The sketch worker has no DOM canvas; OffscreenCanvas with a 2D context works in workers. Decode with createImageBitmap(canvas, { imageOrientation: 'flipY' }) so the drawing stands upright, as three.js flips it.

entries.target: After 1.0: engine.registerVideo on the page and textures.fromVideo in the sketch. Until then, send ImageBitmap frames from the page and call texture.update(bitmap)
entries.notes: The ImageBitmap route decodes and uploads every frame, so keep frames small (null3d-develop recipe 14).

entries.target: assets.loadCubemap(urls) for sky boxes; assets.loadEnvironment for lighting
`bunx @null3d/cli assets env studio.hdr` offline, then assets.loadEnvironment
entries.notes: Prefiltering happens once at build time instead of on every visit.

entries.target: assets.loadTexture('x.ktx2')
entries.notes: Built in; delete the setup.

entries.three: texture.channel (which UV set a map uses)
entries.target: uvSet: 0 or 1 in loadTexture options, or per map in the material
entries.notes: glTF files carry this per texture, so loaded models need nothing.

entries.target: loadTexture(url, { premultipliedAlpha: true }), which multiplies each color by its alpha as the image decodes
entries.notes: Standard blending needs no flag.

entries.target: const prefab = await assets.loadGltf(url); scene.instantiate(prefab)
entries.notes: Animations are in prefab.animations; named nodes via prefab.find(name).

entries.target: Draco files load, but convert them to meshopt with `bunx @null3d/cli assets optimize`
entries.notes: meshopt decodes faster and needs no separate decoder download.

entries.target: Built in
entries.notes: Delete the setup.

entries.three: FBXLoader / OBJLoader / MTLLoader / ColladaLoader / STLLoader / PLYLoader / 3DMLoader / USDZLoader
entries.target: Convert to glTF before release (`bunx @null3d/cli assets convert`, or Blender)
entries.notes: The engine loads glTF only.

entries.target: assets.onProgress((loaded, total) => ...) and assets.preload([...urls])
assets.loadBinary(url), assets.loadJson(url), assets.loadImageBitmap(url)
Nothing to do
entries.notes: Loads of one URL at the same time share one download, files that assets.preload downloaded wait in memory until a load takes them, and the HTTP cache keeps the rest.

entries.target: scene.createInstances(meshOrPrefab, count, { material, dynamic }); write batch.positions / rotations / scales / colors
entries.notes: Static batches call markDirty(start, count) after writes; dynamic batches upload every frame without it.

entries.target: Nothing special: the engine batches objects that share a mesh and material
entries.notes: Use createInstances for many copies of one mesh, and separate meshes for varied geometry.

entries.target: createInstances(mesh, count, { material, attributes: { tint: 4 } }) adds per-instance arrays that surface functions can read
scene.createLod({ levels: [{ mesh, distance }] }), or LODs generated by `bunx @null3d/cli assets optimize --lod`
entries.notes: The engine picks levels on job workers or on the GPU, per instance.

entries.three: AnimationMixer / clipAction / play / crossFadeTo / fadeIn / fadeOut / setEffectiveWeight / timeScale / mixer.update(dt)
entries.target: const anim = obj.animator(); anim.play('run', { fade: 0.2, loop: true, speed }); anim.crossFade('walk', 0.3); anim.setLayerWeight(layer, w)
entries.notes: No update call: the engine samples animation on job workers.

entries.target: Animate values in onUpdate; transform clips authored in glTF play through the animator (0.2)
entries.notes: Property animation (scene.animateProperty and glTF KHR_animation_pointer) comes after 1.0.

entries.three: SkinnedMesh / Skeleton / Bone built by hand
entries.target: Skins load from glTF; anim.setJointOverride(jointName, rotation) for procedural aiming
entries.notes: Building skeletons in code is not supported; author them in a modeling tool.

entries.target: `bunx @null3d/cli assets` splits clips and makes them additive offline; anim.play(name, { additive: true })
camera.screenToRay(x, y, ray); scene.raycast(ray.origin, ray.direction, { layers }, hit)
entries.notes: Returns the closest hit; scene.raycastAll returns every hit. Acceleration structures are built in.

entries.three: DOM pointer, mouse, touch and keyboard listeners
entries.target: input.pointer, input.isDown('KeyW'), input.wasPressed('Mouse0'), input.touches, input.actions.define(); obj.on('pointerenter' | 'pointerleave' | 'click', fn) (0.2)
entries.notes: The page forwards pointer, touch, keyboard and gamepad input to the sketch, which reads it once per frame and adds no DOM listeners. Keys take KeyboardEvent.code names, and the main mouse button or a tap is Mouse0. A canvas that takes touch gestures needs touch-action: none in its CSS.

entries.target: createOrbitControls(ctx, camera, { target, enableDamping, dampingFactor, minDistance, maxDistance, maxPolarAngle }) from @null3d/controls; controls.update(dt) in onUpdate
entries.notes: Option names match OrbitControls. Trackball and Arcball come after 1.0.

entries.target: createFlyControls / createFirstPersonControls from @null3d/controls
entries.notes: Pointer lock is requested on the page: engine.requestPointerLock().

entries.target: Dragging with scene.raycast against a plane
entries.notes: Gizmos come after 1.0.

entries.three: AxesHelper / GridHelper / BoxHelper / Box3Helper / ArrowHelper / CameraHelper / light helpers / SkeletonHelper / PlaneHelper
entries.target: debug.axes, debug.grid, debug.box, debug.sphere, debug.arrow, debug.frustum, debug.light, debug.skeleton
entries.notes: Call them in onUpdate: each call draws for one frame. Debug drawing exists in development builds only. debug.grid takes GridHelper's size and divisions. debug.skeleton comes with animation in 0.2.

entries.three: new Vector3 / Quaternion / Matrix4 / Euler / Color / Box3 / Sphere / Ray / Plane
entries.target: Plain arrays and the vec3, quat, mat4 and color helpers from @null3d/engine, such as vec3.add(out, a, b) and quat.slerp(out, a, b, t)
entries.notes: Create scratch arrays once with vec3.create(), quat.create() or mat4.create(), outside onUpdate. Most names match three.js. applyQuaternion is vec3.transformQuat, applyMatrix4 is vec3.transformMat4, multiplyScalar is vec3.scale and addScaledVector is vec3.scaleAndAdd. setFromUnitVectors is quat.rotationTo, and setFromEuler is quat.fromEuler, in radians. There are no helpers for Box3, Sphere, Ray or Plane. three.js math classes may stay in setup code during a port, but not in per-frame code.

entries.target: onUpdate(dt) or ctx.time.dt, and ctx.time.now
entries.notes: getDelta() becomes the dt that onUpdate gets, also in ctx.time.dt, and getElapsedTime() becomes ctx.time.now. Sketch time stops while the engine is paused or the page is hidden. A fixed-step simulation, such as world.step(1 / 60), moves to onFixedUpdate.

entries.three: MathUtils (degToRad, clamp, lerp, damp, randFloat, seededRandom)
entries.target: math.degToRad, math.clamp, math.lerp, math.damp, math.randFloat and the other MathUtils names; math.seed and math.random
entries.notes: Same names and arithmetic. The random helpers draw from math.random, which hold mode seeds. MathUtils.seededRandom(s) becomes math.seed(s) once, then math.random().

entries.target: '#rrggbb' or '#rgb' strings, 0xrrggbb numbers, or [r, g, b] sRGB arrays from 0 to 1; color.fromHex, color.fromSrgb and color.fromHsl give linear RGB
entries.notes: Color options take sRGB, and the engine converts them to linear, as three.js does for hex colors. Instance colors are linear, so fill them with the color helpers. three.js's setRGB takes linear values, so convert them with color.linearToSrgb for a color option. color.fromHsl gives what setHSL gives, and vec3.lerp blends two colors.

entries.three: EffectComposer / RenderPass / OutputPass / PostProcessing (three/webgpu) / pmndrs postprocessing
entries.target: post.set({ ... })
entries.notes: The chain is built in and merged into few passes. Delete the composer; keep only each pass's settings.

entries.target: post.set({ bloom: { strength, radius, threshold } })
entries.notes: Similar response to UnrealBloomPass; tune with parity images.

entries.target: post.set({ ao: { radius, intensity } })
entries.notes: GTAO at half resolution, on the High and Ultra presets.

entries.target: Anti-aliasing follows the preset (MSAA or FXAA); post.set({ fxaa: true }) forces FXAA
entries.notes: SMAA and SSAA have no equivalent. TAA comes after 1.0.

entries.target: post.set({ outline: { color, thickness } }) and obj.setOutlined(true)
Skip it, or write a custom final effect (scene depth is available to it)
post.addEffect({ name, wgsl, uniforms })
entries.notes: Rewrite the effect in WGSL; per-pixel effects merge into the final pass for free.

entries.three: FilmPass / GlitchPass / HalftonePass / AfterimagePass / DotScreenPass / RenderPixelatedPass
entries.target: Custom effects with post.addEffect
entries.notes: The cookbook has recipes for film grain, pixelation and afterimage.

entries.target: post.set({ lut: await assets.loadLut('grade.cube') })
The environment map
entries.notes: Planar and screen-space reflections come after 1.0.

entries.target: A water surface function that samples the environment map
